title: Thailand packing guide for women
description: What to wear in Thailand: temples, Bangkok, beaches and nightlife for women. Packing lists by trip length, temple rules and looks at three budgets.
intro: Thailand is hot, humid and busy. You will go from a grand palace to a night market to a beach in one week. Pack quick-dry fabrics, a long layer for temples and shoes that slip on and off. Here are looks, temple rules and packing lists for three, five and seven days.

sections.heading: Temple note
sections.body: At the Grand Palace and at most temples, you must cover your shoulders and knees. Skirts and dresses should reach below the knee. Trousers should not be see-through. Sleeveless tops and shorts will turn you away at the gate. Carry a light shirt or shawl and wear loose trousers or a long skirt. Remove your shoes before entering a building. Do not point your feet at a Buddha statue.
tips: Cover shoulders and knees. No exceptions at the Grand Palace.
Wear slip-on shoes, since you remove them often.
A thin long skirt is cool and temple-ready.
Rent a wrap at the gate if you are caught out, but prices are high.

sections.heading: Outfit formulas
sections.body: Each with footwear and one accessory.

looks.name: Temple day
pieces: Linen or cotton wide trousers, about ₹1,000 (Uniqlo sale, H&M or Myntra)
Short-sleeved shirt in white or sage, about ₹800
looks.why: Covered and cool. Both rules, in one outfit.

looks.name: Bangkok city day
pieces: Viscose midi dress, about ₹2,500 (Zara, Mango or Vero Moda)
looks.why: You walk and use public transport. Comfort wins.

looks.name: Beach day, Phuket or Krabi
pieces: Swimsuit with a kaftan, about ₹2,500 (H&M or Zara)
Accessory: reef-safe sunscreen and sunglasses, about ₹1,000
looks.why: It handles beach, boat and lunch.

looks.name: Rooftop bar night
pieces: Satin or silk dress, about ₹6,500 (Mango, AND or Zara)
looks.why: Rooftop bars in Bangkok are dressy. This look fits.

sections.heading: Packing list by trip length
sections.body: Three days: two dresses, one pair of linen trousers, one shirt, one swimsuit, sandals, sneakers and a scarf. Five days: add a skirt, a second shirt and a night dress. Seven days: add a second swimsuit and a light rain jacket. Markets sell cheap cotton dresses. Leave room in your bag.
tips: Three days: six to seven items.
Pack a small umbrella for sudden showers.

sections.heading: Moving around the country
sections.body: Thailand is easy to move through, but the way you travel changes what you wear. In Bangkok, you take the BTS, the MRT and tuk-tuks. You walk a lot, so shoes matter. In Chiang Mai, you visit temples and markets, and trek in the north, so pack trousers and a light fleece for cool mornings. On the islands, you take boats and wade through water, so pack quick-dry shorts and a dry bag. Domestic flights have luggage limits, often 20 kg, and some budget airlines are stricter. Pack light.
tips: Bangkok: sneakers, light trousers and a cross-body bag.
Chiang Mai: a light fleece for mornings and a rain jacket.
Islands: quick-dry shorts, a dry bag and sliders.
Check the baggage limit on budget flights.

sections.heading: On the plane
sections.body: Wear comfortable leggings or joggers, a long tee and a cardigan. Slip-on shoes help at security. Put a scarf in your bag. It works at a temple on day one.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: November to February is cool and dry, with 24 to 32 degrees. March to May is very hot. June to October is rainy and humid. Pack quick-dry clothes and a rain jacket in the wet season. Islands have their own weather. Check before you go.

sections.heading: Colour and silhouette
sections.body: Thailand is loud, so natural colours look calm. White, sage, cream, sky blue and terracotta suit the humidity. Loose silhouettes in linen and viscose keep you cool. A belt gives shape if you want it. Warm skin tones glow in terracotta and olive. Cool skin tones glow in soft blue, lilac and rose.
tips: Wear dark underlayers if you wear white.
Pick colours that match so you can mix.
Carry a tote for market buys.

sections.heading: What to stop buying for Thailand
sections.body: Stop buying polyester. It traps sweat. Stop buying one-use outfits for photos. Stop buying heavy luggage. Markets sell lovely cotton clothes at low prices. Stop buying shoes you cannot walk in for hours.

faq.q: What should women wear in Thailand?
faq.a: Wear light, quick-dry clothes, and carry a layer for temples. Cover shoulders and knees at religious sites.

faq.q: Can I wear shorts in Bangkok?
faq.a: Yes in the city, but not at the Grand Palace or temples. Carry trousers or a long skirt for those.

faq.q: What shoes should I wear in Thailand?
faq.a: Slip-on sandals and cushioned sneakers. You will take shoes off often.

faq.q: What should I wear to a rooftop bar?
faq.a: A dress or smart co-ord with a light layer. Some bars ask for closed shoes. Check the policy.

cta.headline: Pack once. Wear everything.
cta.sub: One selfie, five questions: your season, your palette, your three strengths. Pack the shades that already suit you. Free.
